the_finding.what: Survival is flat because the gate cannot credit the work, not because the work is absent.
the_finding.one_to_one: Against pass 1, probe 2 fixed +6 more targets correctly and gained +6 unsatisfiable; probe 1 fixed +9 and gained +9. Every additional target the worker gets right becomes an unsatisfiable task rather than a survivor.
the_finding.mechanism: All outside errors land in TEST files — 21 of 21 on probe 1, 0 in non-test source. Tightening a type under --strictNullChecks propagates into fixtures and mocks, and the gate forbids editing tests because tests ARE the gate (ADR-0046). No legal edit passes.
the_finding.perverse_direction: The unsatisfiable count RISES with worker capability (12 -> 18 -> 21), because a file nobody edits cannot break anything downstream.
the_finding.counterfactual_not_claimed: 15 of probe 1's tasks had a clean target with only test-file errors and would have REACHED the suite under different scoping. Whether they would survive it is unmeasured and is not claimed.

threats: The task set was chosen to contain failures, and the strictness setting was chosen too (ADR-0063). No rate here says how often real work hits this shape.

D = 0.105 is the gate's own measured error rate. S14 = 2/30 = 0.067 sits below the 0.10 threshold by less than D, so the branch is taken on a margin narrower than the instrument's own error. The two probes agreeing is what carries the verdict, not the margin.
12 of 30 were already unsatisfiable for the 7B, so the reachable maximum on this task set was never 30/30. The frozen rule is applied to 30 regardless, as written.
